summary: Weak keyword co-occurrence in utility module; no traced installer harm
details: Package sixbails@1.0.4 triggered a single a static rule on lib/Utils/generics.js citing keyword co-occurrence of 'ping', 'GET', and 'id' across widely separated lines (6, 33, 194, 238, 403). No lifecycle scripts, no top-level import-time network activity, no credential-path reads (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, browser stores), no hardcoded attacker endpoint, and no exec of fetched content are cited. The pattern is consistent with an ordinary utility module containing HTTP GET helpers and a 'ping'-shaped identifier or method, not with an exfiltration path against the installer. Without corroborating evidence of a specific installer-side data source flowing to a specific attacker-controlled destination, this is a keyword-proximity match rather than confirmed attack behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
